name: Basal Encephalocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Basal Encephalocele

criteria.description: Presence of a congenital defect in the base of the skull allowing herniation of brain tissue
Identification of herniated brain tissue or meninges through the skull base defect on imaging
Clinical signs such as nasal obstruction, cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea, or midline nasal mass
MRI or CT confirmation of encephalocele location and contents
Exclusion of other craniofacial malformations or syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a congenital skull base defect with herniation of brain tissue confirmed by imaging and compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically soft, compressible, and may increase with crying or straining
Clear nasal discharge due to CSF leakage
searchTerms: leakage of spinal fluid from nose

pathognomonic.notes: Defect in the anterior cranial fossa or sphenoid bone
searchTerms: hole or gap in skull base present at birth

common.notes: Due to mass effect of the encephalocele
Secondary to CSF leakage and infection

occasional.notes: Due to optic nerve involvement or mass effect
May occur if brain tissue is involved
Altered nasal shape due to mass

rare.notes: Occasionally due to CSF flow obstruction
Rare involvement of adjacent cranial nerves
searchTerms: cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.notes: Due to airway obstruction in large lesions

laboratory: Analysis of nasal discharge for beta-2 transferrin to confirm CSF leak
imaging: MRI showing herniation of brain tissue through skull base defect
CT scan demonstrating bony defect in anterior cranial fossa or sphenoid bone
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Physical examination revealing midline nasal mass and nasal obstruction

distinguishingFeatures: Imaging shows cystic lesion without brain tissue
No skull base defect on imaging

references: Radiographics. Basal Encephaloceles: Imaging and Clinical Features. 2019.
Journal of Neurosurgery: Management of Basal Encephaloceles in Children. 2021.
